speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, everyone.
zh: 大家好。

speaker: Unknown
en: My name is Gabriel Martinez.
zh: 我叫 Gabriel Martinez。

speaker: Unknown
en: I go by Gabo.
zh: 大家叫我 Gabo。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm an engineering manager and resident slop warden at G2i, and I'm here to talk about slop.
zh: 我是 G2i 的工程经理兼常驻 slop 看门人，我今天要讲的是 slop。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm here to talk about slop because I'm rather passionate about the topic.
zh: 我之所以要讲 slop,是因为我对这个话题相当有热情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by passionate, I mean angry.
zh: 说是有热情，其实是愤怒。

speaker: Unknown
en: The term slop has been beaten to a pulp, but the thing it points at has long been around.
zh: “slop”这个词已经被用烂了，但它所指的东西其实早就存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: Only now it happens at warp speed.
zh: 只不过现在它以光速发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Slop is what happens when generation outruns judgment.
zh: Slop 就是生成速度超过判断速度时产生的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: Slop is not AI-generated code.
zh: Slop 不是指 AI 生成的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't mean to define it as some concrete objective thing that can easily be sniffed out, although there are tells.
zh: 我并不是要把它定义成某种可以轻易被嗅探出来的具体客观事物，尽管它确实有一些特征。

speaker: Unknown
en: Slop is output that looks finished before the thinking is finished.
zh: Slop 是那种在思考还没完成之前就看起来已经完工的产出。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is work product where ambiguity was cleared with guesses, where trade-offs were left to chance, where ownership was not taken.
zh: 它是这样的工作成果：歧义靠猜测来消除，权衡随缘，责任无人承担。

speaker: Unknown
en: Output was produced, sure, but understanding was not.
zh: 产出确实有了，但理解并没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the real danger is not simply that the machine made a bad choice.
zh: 而真正的危险不只是机器做出了一个糟糕的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: The danger is that the engineer never noticed that there was a choice to make.
zh: 危险在于工程师从未意识到那里原本存在一个需要做的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: They never hit the ambiguity.
zh: 他们从未撞上那个歧义。

speaker: Unknown
en: They never felt the constraint.
zh: 他们从未感受到那个约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: They never discovered the edge case that would have changed the design.
zh: 他们从未发现那个本会改变设计的边界情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: The work arrived already smoothed over.
zh: 工作成果到达时就已经被抹平了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with it, the unknown unknowns stayed unknown.
zh: 随之而来的是，未知的未知依然是未知的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But software is a record of choices, technical choices, product choices, operational choices, user-facing choices.
zh: 但软件就是一份选择记录——技术选择、产品选择、运维选择、面向用户的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we do not see those choices, we cannot own them.
zh: 如果我们看不到这些选择，我们就无法为它们负责。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we do not own them, we are not really engineering.
zh: 而如果我们不为它们负责，我们就不是在真正地做工程。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are just accepting output.
zh: 我们只是在接受产出。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are just a code monkey hitting the merge button.
zh: 我们只是一只按下合并按钮的代码猴。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not the purist that's come here to tell you that AI is bad.
zh: 我不是那种跑来告诉你 AI 很糟糕的纯粹主义者。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not bad, OK?
zh: 它并不糟糕，好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm here to describe some of the patterns that have led to our drunken AI stupor.
zh: 我在这里是要描述一些导致我们陷入这场 AI 醉酒般迷醉状态的模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's absolutely understandable, given the advancements made since December 25, how we got to where we are.
zh: 鉴于自 2025 年 12 月以来取得的进步，我们能走到今天这一步是完全可以理解的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we need to dial it in.
zh: 但我们需要把它校准好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to slow down.
zh: 我们需要慢下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to sober up.
zh: 我们需要清醒过来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Agents can seem to make magic, and the internet would make you believe it is so.
zh: 智能体看起来能创造魔法，而互联网也会让你相信确实如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can write code, scaffold screens, and with right tuning can build whole features or systems.
zh: 它们能写代码、搭建界面，经过恰当调校还能构建完整的功能或系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they cannot replace the human work of deciding what matters, understanding what is being built, interpreting ambiguity, owning the system for the long haul, exercising judgment and restraint at the system architecture level, and arguably the most important, knowing what not to build.
zh: 但它们无法取代人类的工作：决定什么才是重要的、理解正在构建的是什么、解读歧义、长期为系统负责、在系统架构层面行使判断力和克制——以及可以说最重要的，知道什么不该构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: Slop is not about AI as a tool.
zh: Slop 与 AI 这个工具无关。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rather, it is about the absence of judgment.
zh: 相反，它关乎判断力的缺席。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's talk a little bit about what got us here.
zh: 那么让我们稍微聊聊我们是怎么走到这一步的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In a world where anything is possible, deciding what to build is more important than ever.
zh: 在一个一切皆有可能的世界里，决定构建什么比以往任何时候都更重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: People have gotten overly excited and built behemoths of spaghetti product nonsense.
zh: 人们过度兴奋，构建出了意大利面式产品胡言乱语的庞然大物。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's almost as if they've forgotten that any line of code you write is a liability, that the best code is no code at all.
zh: 他们几乎忘了你写的每一行代码都是一种负债，忘了最好的代码就是根本没有代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: The cost of creating code is falling, but the cost of understanding a software program is not.
zh: 创建代码的成本在下降，但理解一个软件程序的成本并没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I want to be clear here.
zh: 这里我想说清楚一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not saying every line of code needs to be personally read, blessed, and understood in isolation.
zh: 我不是说每一行代码都需要被亲自阅读、核准并孤立地理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: That has never really been the standard.
zh: 这从来都不是真正的标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: Large systems have always contained more detail than any one person can hold in their head.
zh: 大型系统所包含的细节，从来都超过任何一个人脑能装下的量。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the logic has to be understood.
zh: 但逻辑必须被理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: The main flows, the boundaries, the data model and product behaviors have to be understood.
zh: 主要流程、边界、数据模型和产品行为必须被理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good software has a kind of harmony to it, not in some precious aesthetic sense, in a practical sense.
zh: 好的软件有一种和谐感，不是某种矫情的审美意义上的，而是实用意义上的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The code should reflect the shape of the domain.
zh: 代码应该反映领域的形状。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI can generate code, but it cannot magically give a messy system coherence.
zh: AI 可以生成代码，但它无法神奇地给一个混乱的系统带来连贯性。

speaker: Unknown
en: An agent can operate with much more effectively inside a code base that has structure, patterns, clear boundaries, and rationale.
zh: 一个智能体在一个有结构、有模式、有清晰边界和理据的代码库中运行会有效得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if the system is already a big ball of mud, the agent does not rescue you from the mud.
zh: 但如果系统已经是一团泥球，智能体并不能把你从泥潭中拯救出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just builds the ball bigger, faster.
zh: 它只会把泥球堆得更大、更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just because you can generate another component does not mean the product needs another component.
zh: 仅仅因为你能再生成一个组件，并不意味着产品需要再一个组件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dykstra had this great line.
zh: Dykstra 有过一句很棒的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we could count lines of code, we would not think of them as lines produced but as lines spent.
zh: 如果我们能统计代码行数，我们不应把它们看作产出的行，而应看作花费的行。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is the cost of building.
zh: 这是构建的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI makes it easier to spend lines.
zh: AI 让花掉代码行变得更容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes it easier to spend on files, abstractions, and complexity.
zh: 它让在文件、抽象和复杂度上花钱变得更容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: But at the end of the day, you own the bill.
zh: 但归根结底，账单由你来付。

speaker: Unknown
en: That build shows up as confusion, brittle flows, features nobody wants to touch because they don't fully understand.
zh: 那些构建以困惑、脆弱的流程、没人想碰的特性(因为没人完全理解它们)的形式显现出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It shows up as product surfaces that technically do everything but feel like a maze.
zh: 它显现为在技术上什么都能做、但感觉像迷宫的产品表面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think about that special kind of bloated B2B software where every task requires training, where every screen has 12 escape hatches and nobody can explain whether the complexity is there because users needed it or because teams just kept adding things.
zh: 想想那种特殊的臃肿 B2B 软件，每个任务都需要培训，每个屏幕有 12 个逃生出口，而且没人能解释这些复杂度到底是因为用户需要，还是因为团队只是一直在往上堆东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Teams should be held accountable for work they are producing.
zh: 团队应该为他们产出的工作被问责。

speaker: Unknown
en: Accountability is the key word here.
zh: 问责是这里的关键词。

speaker: Unknown
en: Taking ownership over the product you're building and having a way to tie that to positive or negative reinforcement.
zh: 对你正在构建的产品负起责任，并有一种方式把这与正向或负向的强化挂钩。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just in the mere fact of knowing that someone else will review your work will force engineers to pay just a little bit more attention to the finer details and be a bit more meticulous, especially if there are accountability metrics that can be made visible for each chunk of work product.
zh: 仅仅知道会有别人审查你的工作这一点，就会迫使工程师对细节多花一点心思、更一丝不苟，尤其是当每个工作产物块都有可以被公开的问责指标时。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're entering the age of bloated products with Spaghetti UX on the order of worst kinds of B2B ERPs you may have ever been trained to use.
zh: 我们正在进入一个臃肿产品加意大利面条式 UX 的时代，其糟糕程度堪比你可能被培训使用过的最糟糕的那类 B2B ERP。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, anyone can Vibecode an application in an hour and end up with a working clickable prototype.
zh: 今天，任何人都能在一小时内 Vibecode 出一个应用，最终得到一个可点击的可用原型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that has changed expectations.
zh: 而这改变了预期。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because once people see software appear that quickly, they start to believe software can be built that quickly.
zh: 因为一旦人们看到软件出现得这么快，他们就开始相信软件可以被造得这么快。

speaker: Unknown
en: They see a few prompts turn into screens.
zh: 他们看到几个 prompt 变成了屏幕。

speaker: Unknown
en: They see a terminal session produce something that looks real.
zh: 他们看到一次终端会话产出了看起来很真实的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to be fair, sometimes it is real enough to be useful.
zh: 平心而论，有时候它确实真实到足以有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes that prototype is a great way to explore an idea.
zh: 有时候那个原型是探索一个想法的好方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the problem is that stakeholders that do not live in the codebase often experience that prototype as evidence that the hard part is over.
zh: 但问题在于，不生活在代码库里的利益相关者常常把那个原型体验为「难的部分已经结束了」的证据。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not thinking about the parts where real battle-hardened engineers are in their keep.
zh: 他们没有想到真正的身经百战的工程师所坚守的那些部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's outside the happy path, figuring out how to cohesively integrate a new feature set, the work involved in clarifying requirements, the work of actually manually testing a feature set to ensure that it works, as a human should expect,
zh: 那些部分在快乐路径之外：想清楚如何把一个新特性集合连贯地集成进来、澄清需求所涉及的工作、真正手动测试一个特性集合以确保它能正常工作的活，就像一个人类应该期望的那样，

speaker: Unknown
en: And that the UX isn't complete garbage.
zh: 以及确保 UX 不是彻底的垃圾。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not at all thinking about the most time-consuming bits, the human parts, the last mile, where the judgment lives.
zh: 他们完全没想到最耗时的部分，也就是人的部分、最后一公里，判断力所在的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is where someone has to read the code, test the behavior, own the trade-offs, notice the missing requirements, and decide whether this thing deserves to be a part of the system.
zh: 在这里，必须有人去读代码、测试行为、为取舍负责、注意到缺失的需求，并决定这个东西是否值得成为系统的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's a tweet that emphasizes the point I'm trying to make here.
zh: 这有一条推文，强调了我在这里想表达的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It quotes the creator of SQLite, who on the topic of pull requests says, you say, oh, it's free.
zh: 它引用了 SQLite 的创造者，关于 pull request 的话题，他说：你说，哦，这是免费的。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, it's not free.
zh: 不，它不免费。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you're doing is asking me to maintain it for you, to document it for you, to test it for you, to maintain it for you for the next 25 years.
zh: 你在做的,是要求我为你维护它、为你写文档、为你测试它、为你维护它 25 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is not free.
zh: 那不是免费的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this really struck a chord with me.
zh: 这真的引起了我的强烈共鸣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I couldn't have said it better.
zh: 我说不出比这更好的话了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's easy to yeet of PR, but who has to own that thing?
zh: 随手 yeet 一个 PR 很容易，但谁来拥有那个东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: Who's responsible for the repercussions of what that means?
zh: 谁来为它所意味的后果负责？

speaker: Unknown
en: So external pressures from stakeholders coupled with pressures of competing with slopmeisters begets mucho slopo.
zh: 于是，来自利益相关者的外部压力，再加上与 slop 高手竞争的压力，催生出海量的 slop。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure most of you have seen this in the wild, where the bad engineers, the ones who don't review the details, that don't refine the spec, that aren't detail-oriented, end up producing more faster.
zh: 我相信你们大多数人都在现实中见过这种情况：那些糟糕的工程师，那些不审查细节、不打磨 spec、不注重细节的人，最终产出得更多更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: The folks who pay attention to the detail and go above and beyond are the ones that might seem like they're doing less and moving slower.
zh: 而那些注重细节、并且做得超出预期的人，反而可能看起来做得更少、移动得更慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: How this propagates is it yields performance anxiety, wherein team environments can pressure engineers to merge PRs faster than they can judge, leading to code being merged without full understanding.
zh: 这种情况如何传导呢？它产生绩效焦虑：在团队环境中，工程师可能被迫在还能做出判断之前就更快地合并 PR，导致代码在没有完全理解的情况下被合并。

speaker: Unknown
en: Short-term thinking, getting that PR in wins over long-term code health.
zh: 短期思维：把那个 PR 合进去，胜过了长期的代码健康。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've personally felt this anxiety where engineers around me were merging at an incredible pace, and I felt constant anxiety that I was not moving fast enough.
zh: 我个人就感受过这种焦虑，当时我周围的工程师以惊人的速度合并代码，而我持续地焦虑自己移动得不够快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I can admit that it led me to merge code that I didn't necessarily review with a level of detail that I normally do or should have.
zh: 我可以承认，这导致我合并了一些我并没有以通常的细致程度、或本应有的细致程度去审查的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've seen horror stories of people merging code they don't fully understand or haven't even tested themselves.
zh: 我见过很多恐怖故事,有人合并了自己不完全理解、甚至自己都没测试过的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the end of the day, we're all human.
zh: 说到底,我们都是人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are driven by incentive.
zh: 我们都被激励驱动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if incentives are driving people to get PRs in, then we're going to be in for a rude awakening.
zh: 如果激励驱使人们尽快提交 PR,那我们迟早会遭到残酷的清醒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rewards should be centered around producing value, elegant, well-factored, pragmatic system design, and around clarity of test and evaluation harnesses.
zh: 奖励应该围绕着创造价值、优雅的、良好拆分的、务实的系统设计,以及清晰的测试与评估框架。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's just something that really grinds my gears about seeing a multi-thousand line PR.
zh: 看到一个几千行的 PR,真的让我特别恼火。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no way in hell that a human can fully understand all the important bits of a change that big.
zh: 人类根本不可能完全理解这么大的改动中所有重要的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is our job as engineers to optimize for this new world, to decompose needs into its simplest chunks, which lends to understanding, understanding simpler code surfaces and controlling of our code bases.
zh: 作为工程师,我们的工作就是为这个新世界做优化,把需求分解成最简单的块,这样才能便于理解、理解更简单的代码表面,并掌控我们的代码库。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI is supposed to have been eradicating jobs, and engineers are supposed to be moving at the rate of token production.
zh: AI 本应该已经在消灭工作岗位,工程师本应该以 token 生产的速度前进。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there is a lot of pressure to be producing more faster.
zh: 所以有巨大的压力要更快地产出更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: What AI is really doing is producing more faster, more characters that eat more human time.
zh: 而 AI 真正在做的是更快地产出更多,产出更多消耗人类时间的字符。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've seen this happen in the most mundane ways.
zh: 我见过这种情况以最平凡的方式发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: You give someone 10 bullets of scope, a few user journeys, something intentionally lightweight, and they come back with a 20-page document.
zh: 你给某人 10 条范围要点、几个用户旅程,刻意保持轻量的东西,结果他们交回来一份 20 页的文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe it looks polished with fancy prose, but now I have to spend hours figuring out whether there's any real thinking inside it.
zh: 也许它看起来很精致,辞藻华丽,但现在我得花好几个小时去弄清楚里面到底有没有真正的思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is AI-generated work in the worst sense.
zh: 这就是最糟糕意义上的 AI 生成的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: It does not clarify the problem.
zh: 它没有把问题厘清。

speaker: Unknown
en: It expanded it.
zh: 它把问题扩大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It took ambiguity that should have been resolved by the person doing the work and handed it back as a larger artifact for other stakeholders to do it.
zh: 它把本该由做事的人解决的模糊性,变成一个更大的产物扔回来,让其他利益相关者去解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: In code, a vague task becomes a large PR.
zh: 在代码中,一个模糊的任务会变成一个巨大的 PR。

speaker: Unknown
en: A small feature becomes a pile of files.
zh: 一个小功能会变成一堆文件。

speaker: Unknown
en: The output arrives with the shape of completion, but the real work has just moved to the reviewer.
zh: 产出以「完成」的形态送达,但真正的工作只是转移到了评审者身上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is the part that we need to be honest about.
zh: 而这正是我们需要诚实面对的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Generation is cheap, but evaluation is expensive.
zh: 生成是便宜的,但评估是昂贵的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If AI produces more than humans can possibly evaluate, it has not accelerated the team.
zh: 如果 AI 产出的东西超出人类可能评估的范围,那它并没有加速团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has created a bottleneck.
zh: 它制造了一个瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing that I find particularly annoying is Twitter.
zh: 有一件事让我特别烦,那就是 Twitter。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've got all these self-proclaimed experts and clickbaiters summarizing some talk or promoting some truths that we've always known as if they're some novel genius idea.
zh: 那里有各种自称专家的人和标题党,总结某场演讲,或者把一些我们早就知道的常识当作什么新奇的天才想法来推销。

speaker: Unknown
en: The RLHF loop was one of those.
zh: RLHF 循环就是其中之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was made to sound like a novel agentic breakthrough when it's just a while loop.
zh: 它被说得像什么新奇的智能体突破,其实不过是个 while 循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: Somehow, we've completely forgotten that lines of code is a garbage metric for productivity, but then we decided that it's different than deciding the engineer who burns the most tokens must be producing the most.
zh: 不知怎么的,我们完全忘了代码行数是一个糟糕的生产力指标,然后我们又认定「烧掉最多 token 的工程师一定产出最多」,这和代码行数指标又有什么区别呢。

speaker: Unknown
en: We used to break a feature into small atomic pieces we could reason about, small enough to hold in your head and actually review.
zh: 我们过去会把一个功能拆成小的、可以推理的原子块,小到可以装在脑子里、真正去评审。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we type two sentences and expect a whole not fully thought out feature set back in one shot without really understanding what it is we're asking for.
zh: 现在我们敲两句句子,就指望一次性得到一整套没有充分思考过的功能,却没有真正理解自己要的是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: The key point I want to highlight here is that we do not forget the ground truths we've always known.
zh: 我想在这里强调的关键点是:我们不要忘记我们一直都知道的底层真理。

speaker: Unknown
en: 60 years of software wisdom hasn't been invalidated by AI.
zh: 60 年的软件智慧并没有被 AI 作废。

speaker: Unknown
en: Composable code, good patterns, and solid practices remain essential.
zh: 可组合的代码、好的模式和扎实的实践依然至关重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: A friend recently challenged me on why I spend so much time thinking about guardrails for agents, coding conventions, architectural styles, and constraints around how the system should be shaped.
zh: 最近一位朋友质疑我,为什么我花那么多时间思考智能体的护栏、编码规范、架构风格,以及围绕系统应如何成形的约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: His question was basically, what's the point?
zh: 他的问题基本上是:这有什么意义?

speaker: Unknown
en: If the agent writes the code, why should we care about what the code looks like?
zh: 如果代码是智能体写的,我们为什么还要在乎代码长什么样?

speaker: Unknown
en: And to an extent, I agree.
zh: 在某种程度上,我同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: There will eventually be a world where much implementation detail is completely abstracted away from humans.
zh: 最终会有一天,大量实现细节对人类完全抽象化。

speaker: Unknown
en: That has been the direction of software from the beginning.
zh: 这一直是软件自始至终的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: We went from machine code to assembly, which another level of abstraction up got us to C, then Java, then languages like Ruby, where the primary design goal was programmer happiness.
zh: 我们从机器码到汇编,再往上一层抽象到了 C,然后是 Java,再然后是 Ruby 这类语言,它们的首要设计目标是程序员的幸福感。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just like in languages we built abstractions for garbage collection and manual pointers, AI is abstracting away the imperative bits.
zh: 就像我们在语言中为垃圾回收和手动指针构建了抽象一样,AI 正在把命令式的部分抽象掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: It does not remove the need to understand how a system comes together cohesively.
zh: 但它并没有消除理解一个系统如何凝聚在一起的需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is why diagrams matter so much, not as decorative documentation after the fact, but as a way of making systems legible.
zh: 这就是为什么图示如此重要——不是作为事后装饰性的文档,而是作为让系统变得可读的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: When agents can generate thousands of lines of implementation detail, humans need a compressed review surface, service boundaries, data flows, state transitions, and failure modes.
zh: 当智能体能生成成千上万行实现细节时,人类需要一个压缩的评审表面:服务边界、数据流、状态转换和故障模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: A good diagram lets us see the shape of the system in a way code often obscures.
zh: 一张好的图能让我们看到系统的形状,而代码往往会把它遮蔽。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can leave the main process or workflow as the reviewable surface with implementation details pushed to the leaves.
zh: 我们可以把主流程或工作流留作可评审的表面,把实现细节推到叶子节点。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is why I vouch for declarative code and architecture patterns that create layers humans can actually reason about.
zh: 这就是为什么我支持声明式代码和能创建人类真正可以推理的层次的架构模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: The goal is not just code generation.
zh: 目标不仅仅是代码生成。

speaker: Unknown
en: The goal is human knowledge, human understanding, and human review.
zh: 目标是人类的知识、人类的理解,以及人类的审查。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to optimize for that human layer.
zh: 我们需要为那个人类层面进行优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cognitive overhead is a tax every engineer has to pay before they can make a meaningful change.
zh: 认知开销是每个工程师在做出有意义的改动之前都必须支付的一笔税。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is the time spent figuring out where code belongs, which pattern to follow, and what proper implementation actually means.
zh: 它是花在弄清楚代码应该放在哪里、该遵循哪种模式、以及合理的实现到底意味着什么上的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI does not remove this tax.
zh: AI 并没有消除这笔税。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unless tamed, it exacerbates it.
zh: 如果不加约束,它反而会加剧这笔税。

speaker: Unknown
en: An agent can generate five plausible patterns in five different styles.
zh: 一个智能体可以用五种不同的风格生成五种看似合理的模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now the human reviewer has to reverse engineer not just the code, but the intent behind it.
zh: 而现在人类审查者不仅要对代码进行逆向工程,还要对代码背后的意图进行逆向工程。

speaker: Unknown
en: With proper conventions, intent is more easily rocked.
zh: 有了恰当的约定,意图就更容易被理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: The answer to this is conventions, standards, documented flows, small reviewable surfaces, and clear ownership boundaries and definitions of done.
zh: 答案就是约定、标准、有文档记录的流程、小而可审查的改动面、清晰的所有权边界,以及「完成」的定义。

speaker: Unknown
en: The more obvious the path, the less room there is for slop to hide.
zh: 路径越明确,slop 可藏身的空间就越小。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to give special recognition here to Rails and its place in my heart.
zh: 我想在这里特别致意 Rails,以及它在我心中的位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rails matters here because it shows what happens when a framework aggressively reduces decision surface.
zh: Rails 在这里很重要,因为它展示了一个框架在强力削减决策面时会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: When conventions reduce your overhead, rather than ending up with 10 different ways to structure the same concept, you end up with one.
zh: 当约定降低了你的开销,你最终得到的不是用 10 种不同方式来组织同一个概念,而是只有一种。

speaker: Unknown
en: It may not be perfect in everyone's subjective opinion, but it's understood and it works.
zh: 在每个人的主观看法里它未必完美,但它被理解,而且行之有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: In my career between my first and second forays with Rails, I had a gap of four years.
zh: 在我的职业生涯中,在我第一次和第二次接触 Rails 之间,有四年的空档。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was beautiful to come back after that gap to see that the same patterns in de facto libraries were still the same patterns in de facto libraries.
zh: 隔了那段时间之后回来,看到事实标准库里同样的模式仍然是事实标准库里同样的模式,这很美好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could hop right back into a code base and immediately understand intent without needing to parse through architecture.
zh: 我可以直接跳回一个代码库,立刻理解意图,而不需要去解析架构。

speaker: Unknown
en: It allows engineers to easily move between projects laterally with minimal ramp up.
zh: 它让工程师能够以最小的上手成本,轻松地在项目之间横向移动。

speaker: Unknown
en: The same can be said about other language ecosystems.
zh: 同样的道理也适用于其他语言生态。

speaker: Unknown
en: JavaScript.
zh: JavaScript。

speaker: Unknown
en: Environments with a single correct way of doing things are superior for agentic development because agents aren't confused by dozens of competing approaches.
zh: 拥有单一正确做事方式的环境对智能体开发更优越,因为智能体不会被几十种相互竞争的方法搞得困惑。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is well supported by the official Rails doctrine.
zh: 这一点在 Rails 官方教义中得到了充分支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: It explicitly names optimized for programmer happiness and convention over configuration as core pillars and describes convention as a way to eliminate recurring decisions and lowering the barrier to getting started.
zh: 它明确把「为程序员的幸福感而优化」和「约定优于配置」列为核心支柱,并把约定描述为一种消除重复决策、降低入门门槛的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is the reduction of cognitive overhead.
zh: 这就是认知开销的削减。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything I've talked about today is what led us to build ORC, not only because we think the answer is more agents, and definitely not because we think engineering judgment can be automated away.
zh: 我今天讲的一切,正是引导我们构建 ORC 的原因——不仅因为我们认为答案是更多的智能体,也绝对不是因为我们认为工程判断力可以被自动化掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: We built ORC because we kept seeing the same failure pattern.
zh: 我们构建 ORC,是因为我们不断看到同一种失败模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI could generate code, but the surrounding discipline was still missing.
zh: AI 能够生成代码,但周围的纪律仍然缺失。

speaker: Unknown
en: The planning, the review, the adversarial checks, the context management.
zh: 规划、审查、对抗性检查、上下文管理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Over time, we found ourselves repeating the same human processes to fight slop, break down the work, manage context, weigh out your options, and make sure the output enters the code base in the way the team can still reason about.
zh: 随着时间推移,我们发现自己在一遍遍重复同样的人类流程来对抗 slop——拆解工作、管理上下文、权衡各种选项,并确保产出以一种团队仍然能够推理的方式进入代码库。

speaker: Unknown
en: ORC is taking those lessons and baking them into the workflow.
zh: ORC 就是把这些经验教训固化到工作流中。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is not a magic box that makes correctness disappear as a human responsibility.
zh: 它不是一个让正确性作为人类责任而消失的魔法盒子。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is a system for preserving that responsibility while letting agents do more of the lift.
zh: 它是一个在让智能体承担更多重活的同时,保住那份责任的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: The goal is not to ship more generated code.
zh: 目标不是发布更多生成的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: The goal is to ship software that is still coherent, tested, maintainable, and owned after the generation happens.
zh: 目标是发布在生成发生之后仍然连贯、经过测试、可维护、有人负责的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because the future is not vibe coding better, faster.
zh: 因为未来不是更好、更快地 vibe coding。

speaker: Unknown
en: The future is orchestration with judgment.
zh: 未来是带有判断力的编排。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you all for your time.
zh: 感谢大家的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And remember, don't get sloppy.
zh: 并记住,别变得 sloppy。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll be right back.
zh: 我们马上回来。
